abstract: Abstract A liquid submersion cooling system that is suitable for cooling a number of electronic devices in parallel using a plurality of cases connected to a rack system. The system cools heat-generating components in server computers and other devices that use electronic, heat-generating components and are connected in parallel systems. The system includes a housing having an interior space, a dielectric cooling liquid in the interior space, a heat-generating electronic component disposed within the space and submerged in the dielectric cooling liquid. The rack system contains a manifold system to engage and allow liquid transfer for multiple cases and IO connectors to engage electrically with multiple cases/electronic devices. The rack system can be connected to a pump system for pumping the liquid into and out of the rack, to and from external heat exchangers, heat pumps, or other thermal dissipation/recovery devices.

claims.text: 1. A liquid submersion-cooled server computer array, comprising: a plurality of server computer cases arranged in an array, each case including: a plurality of walls including a lid defining a liquid-tight interior space; a server logic board disposed in the interior space; a plurality of heat generating computer components disposed on the server logic board; a plenum housing within the interior space; the plenum housing includes an inside space, a cooling liquid inlet port in communication with the inside space, and a cooling liquid exit opening in communication with the inside space, and the plenum housing is disposed over one of the heat generating computer components disposed on the server logic board, wherein the plenum housing contains a flow of cooling liquid that is introduced through the cooling liquid inlet port as the cooling liquid flows over the one heat generating computer component toward the cooling liquid exit opening to increase the cooling effectiveness on the one heat generating computer component; a dielectric cooling liquid disposed within the interior space and submerging the plurality of heat generating computer components disposed on the server logic board; a liquid inlet in one of the walls enabling dielectric cooling liquid to enter the case; a liquid outlet in one of the walls enabling dielectric cooling liquid to exit the case; a manifold within the interior space and fluidly connected to the liquid inlet; a tube within the interior space fluidly connected to the manifold and to the cooling liquid inlet port of the plenum housing to direct flow of the dielectric cooling liquid from the manifold into the plenum housing; and a liquid and gas-tight sealed electrical connector extending through one of the walls and electrically connected to the computer components on the server logic board; and a rack system, the plurality of server computer cases of the array are arranged on the rack system.
2. The liquid submersion-cooled server computer array of claim 1, wherein the plurality of server computer cases are arranged in a horizontal array or a vertical array on the rack system.
3. The liquid submersion-cooled server computer array of claim 1, wherein the server computer cases are individually removable from the rack system.

4. The liquid submersion-cooled server computer array of claim 1, wherein the liquid inlet and the liquid outlet each include a quick-disconnect valve that controls the flow of dielectric cooling liquid through the liquid inlet and the liquid outlet respectively; and the rack system includes an inlet manifold that engages the liquid inlet and an outlet manifold that engages the liquid outlet of each case when each case is installed in the rack system, and the inlet manifold and the outlet manifold each include a quick-disconnect valve.

5. The liquid submersion-cooled server computer array of claim 4, wherein the rack system includes a plurality of IO connectors, and the sealed electrical connectors are positioned to engage the IO connectors.
6. The liquid submersion-cooled server computer array of claim 1, wherein the rack system includes a track mechanism that guides installation of the cases onto the rack system.
7. The liquid submersion-cooled server computer array of claim 1, further comprising a lock mechanism to lock the cases to the rack system.
8. The liquid submersion-cooled server computer array of claim 1, wherein the rack system includes a liquid storage tank, a pump, and a heat dissipation device.
9. The liquid submersion-cooled server computer array of claim 1, wherein the sealed electrical connector extends through the lid, and the lid is detachably connected to the case.
10. The liquid submersion-cooled server computer array of claim 1, wherein the array is connected to a coolant liquid system that includes a thermal dissipation device or a thermal recovery device.

11. The liquid submersion-cooled server computer array of claim 1, further comprising a directed flow heat sink connected to the one heat generating computer component, and the directed flow heat sink is disposed within the inside space of the plenum housing.

12. The liquid submersion-cooled server computer array of claim 1, including a liquid coolant flow path in communication with the cases, and the liquid coolant flow path is in heat exchanging relationship with a water cooling loop for cooling liquid coolant flowing in the flow path.

13. A liquid submersion-cooled server computer that is removably attachable in a server computer array, comprising: a housing defining a liquid-tight interior space; a liquid inlet in a wall of the housing, the liquid inlet including a quick-connect valve that controls the flow of liquid through the liquid inlet when the server computer is removed from the server computer array; a liquid outlet in the wall of the housing, the liquid outlet including a quick-connect valve that controls the flow of liquid through the liquid outlet when the server computer is removed from the server computer array; a server logic board disposed in the interior space of the housing, and heat generating electronic devices disposed on the server logic board; a plenum housing within the interior space; the plenum housing includes an inside space, a cooling liquid inlet port in communication with the inside space, and a cooling liquid exit opening in communication with the inside space, and the plenum housing is disposed over one of the heat generating electronic devices disposed on the server logic board, wherein the plenum housing contains a flow of cooling liquid that is introduced through the cooling liquid inlet port as the cooling liquid flows over the one heat generating electronic devices toward the cooling liquid exit opening to increase the cooling effectiveness on the one heat generating electronic device; a dielectric cooling liquid disposed within the interior space and submerging the plurality of heat generating electronic devices disposed on the server logic board; a manifold within the interior space and fluidly connected to the liquid inlet; a tube within the interior space fluidly connected to the manifold and to the plenum housing to direct flow of the dielectric cooling liquid from the manifold into the plenum housing; a heat sink enveloped by the plenum and connected to the one heat generating electronic device; and a liquid and gas-tight sealed IO connector extending through a wall of the housing and electrically connected to the electronic devices on the server logic board.
14. The liquid submersion-cooled server computer of claim 13, wherein the liquid inlet and the liquid outlet are in a back wall of the housing or a bottom wall of the housing.
15. The liquid submersion-cooled server computer of claim 13, wherein the heat generating electronic devices comprise server electronics or processors.
16. The liquid submersion-cooled server computer of claim 13, wherein the sealed IO connector extends through a back wall of the housing or a top wall of the housing.
17. The liquid submersion-cooled server computer of claim 15, comprising a plurality of server logic boards disposed within the interior space.
18. The liquid submersion-cooled server computer of claim 13, wherein the heat generating electronic devices comprise a power supply.
